properties.name: Pegunungan Barisan (Bukit Barisan Mountain System)
properties.description: ~1,700 km long spine mountain system of Sumatra, formed by Cenozoic magmatic arc activity and oblique plate convergence along the Sunda-Java trench.
properties.rock_type: Granitoid batholiths, andesite-dacite volcanics, pre-Tertiary metamorphic basement
properties.evidence_description: Continuous high-relief fault-bounded mountain belt traversing Sumatra with dissected volcanic massifs and pull-apart basins along the Great Sumatran Fault.
properties.evidence_significance: Represents the primary morphotectonic backbone of Sumatra, illustrating magmatic arc evolution and strike-slip terrane deformation.
properties.why_it_matters: The Barisan Mountains host major active geothermal systems, mineralized plutonic complexes, and active tectonic fault grabens across Sumatra.
properties.source: Barber, Crow & Milsom (2005) 'Sumatra: Geology, Resources and Tectonic Evolution' (Geol. Soc. London Memoir 31) & Van Bemmelen (1949)
properties.geometry_note: Polygon envelope represents generalized macro-physiographic mountain province (interface visual convention, not official cadastral survey vector).

properties.name: Pegunungan Meratus (Meratus Suture & Ophiolite Complex)
properties.description: Uplifted Cretaceous subduction-accretion complex and ophiolitic suture belt in South Kalimantan, separating the Barito and Asem-Asem basins.
properties.rock_type: Serpentinized peridotite, gabbro, pillow basalt, radiolarian chert, schist
properties.evidence_description: Exposed Mesozoic ultramafic ophiolite sequence and high-pressure blueschist metamorphic blocks thrust over continental basement.
properties.evidence_significance: Crucial suture zone marking Cretaceous collision between the Schwaner/Sundaland block and East Java-Paternoster microcontinent.
properties.why_it_matters: Exposes Earth mantle rocks and paleo-subduction mélange in Kalimantan, fundamental for SE Asian paleogeographic reconstructions.
properties.source: Sikumbang (1986) 'Geology and Tectonic History of the Meratus Complex' & Wakita et al. (1998)
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary derived from regional geological sheet mapping of Meratus ultramafic outcrop footprint.

properties.name: Pegunungan Selatan Jawa (Southern Mountains Zone)
properties.description: Classic physiographic zone of Java established by Van Bemmelen (1949), comprising Oligo-Miocene volcanic arc formations (OAF) overlain by Miocene limestones.
properties.rock_type: Old Andesite Formation (OAF) breccia, dacitic tuff, Wonosari limestone
properties.evidence_description: Continuous uplifted plateau and rugged coastal ranges forming the southern structural flank of Java.
properties.evidence_significance: Preserves the ancient Paleogene volcanic arc before the subduction zone migrated to its modern Quaternary volcanic axis.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides key stratigraphical record of the transition from ancient volcanic arc activity to extensive carbonate platform deposition.
properties.location_province: Jawa (Jawa Barat, DIY, Jawa Tengah, Jawa Timur)
properties.source: Van Bemmelen (1949) 'The Geology of Indonesia' & Smyth et al. (2008) Geol. Soc. London Spec. Publ. 311
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary represents Van Bemmelen (1949) Southern Mountains Zone regional physiographic envelope.

properties.name: Pegunungan Kendeng (Kendeng Fold-Thrust Belt)
properties.description: East-west trending fold-and-thrust belt in Central-East Java, formed by intense Plio-Pleistocene compression of a deep marine volcaniclastic trough.
properties.rock_type: Turbiditic sandstone, marl, volcaniclastic flysch (Kerek, Kalibeng, Pucangan formations)
properties.evidence_description: Series of asymmetric anticlines, synclines, and south-verging blind thrust faults (Kendeng Thrust).
properties.evidence_significance: Demonstrates active crustal shortening and sedimentary basin inversion within the back-arc realm of Java.
properties.why_it_matters: The Kendeng Zone hosts significant onshore petroleum potential and active blind thrust seismic hazard sources in Java.
properties.source: Van Bemmelen (1949) & de Genevraye and Samuel (1972) Indonesian Petroleum Association
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary reflects the structural anticlinorium footprint between the Randublatung depression and Central volcanic depression.

properties.name: Pegunungan Maoke (Central Range of Papua)
properties.description: Parent Central Cordillera of Papua spanning ~1,300 km, formed by Neogene collision between the Indo-Australian passive margin and Pacific-Caroline oceanic arcs.
properties.rock_type: Mesozoic-Cenozoic limestone, metamorphic phyllite, porphyry intrusive complexes
properties.evidence_description: Massive alpine fold-thrust mountain belt exceeding 4,800 m elevation with remnant tropical glaciers on Puncak Jaya.
properties.evidence_significance: Prime example of active continent-arc collision orogeny producing highest topography in Australasia and giant porphyry Cu-Au deposits.
properties.why_it_matters: Contains Puncak Jaya (Carstensz Pyramid, 4,884 m) and preserves crucial tectonic records of Australian northern margin collision.
properties.source: Dow et al. (1988) 'Geology of the Irian Jaya Region' (Pusat Penelitian dan Pengembangan Geologi) & Cloos et al. (2005)
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary represents parent Central Cordillera mountain belt; Barisan Sudirman (west) and Jayawijaya (east) are documented constituent sub-ranges.

properties.name: Cekungan Bandung (Bandung Volcano-Tectonic Basin)
properties.description: Quaternary volcano-tectonic intermontane depression surrounded by volcanic edifices and bounded north by Sesar Lembang, site of ancient Lake Bandung.
properties.rock_type: Lacustrine clay, tuffaceous sand, volcanic breccia, peat
properties.evidence_description: Flat basin floor (~650-700 m ASL) surrounded by steep volcanic massifs with well-documented lacustrine terrace deposits.
properties.evidence_significance: Demonstrates volcano-tectonic basin subsidence, ancient lake damming (Danau Purba Bandung), and ongoing intra-arc tectonic deformation.
properties.why_it_matters: Provides paleoenvironmental archive of prehistoric Java and critical geological context for seismic and hydrogeological risk in Bandung Raya.
properties.source: Dam et al. (1996) 'The Late Quaternary Evolution of the Bandung Basin' & Silitonga (1973/2003) Badan Geologi
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary strictly delineates the Quaternary lacustrine and volcano-tectonic depression fill, distinct from administrative groundwater (CAT) boundaries.

properties.name: Cekungan Barito (Barito Sedimentary Basin)
properties.description: Asymmetric Tertiary sedimentary basin in South Kalimantan bounded east by the Meratus thrust front and west by the stable Sunda Shield.
properties.rock_type: Tanjung Formation sandstone/shale, Berai limestone, Warukin coal-bearing sandstone
properties.evidence_description: Thick transgressive-regressive sedimentary sequence (up to 6,000 m) with foreland flexural geometry adjacent to Meratus.
properties.evidence_significance: Classic Indonesian hydrocarbon and coal-bearing sedimentary basin illustrating back-arc rift to foreland basin transition.
properties.why_it_matters: One of Indonesia's most thoroughly studied sedimentary basins, hosting significant energy resources and thick coal seams.
properties.source: Witts et al. (2012) 'The Barito Basin, SE Kalimantan' & Satyana et al. (1999) IPA
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary is based on geological stratigraphic pinch-out and basement structural hinge lines, not commercial oil concession blocks.

properties.name: Karst Gunung Sewu (Gunung Sewu UNESCO Global Geopark)
properties.description: World-benchmark tropical cone karst (kegelkarst) and cockpit karst developed in Middle-Late Miocene Wonosari Formation limestones.
properties.rock_type: Wonosari Formation coral limestone, calcarenite, speleothems
properties.evidence_description: Over 40,000 conical limestone hills, thousands of sinkholes (doline/uvala), and extensive subterranean river networks and caves (Luweng Ombo, Luweng Jaran).
properties.evidence_significance: International type-locality for tropical conical karst geomorphology and Quaternary hominin habitation caves (Song Terus).
properties.why_it_matters: Designated a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2015, Gunung Sewu is a global benchmark for tropical speleology, hydrogeology, and geoheritage.
properties.source: Haryono & Day (2004) 'Landform differentiation within Gunung Sewu kegelkarst' & UNESCO Global Geopark Dossier (2015)
properties.geometry_note: Polygon boundary matches the contiguous Wonosari Formation limestone plateau and UNESCO Global Geopark boundary.

properties.name: Palung Sunda-Jawa (Sunda-Java Subduction Trench)
properties.description: ~3,000 km oceanic subduction trench (depth 6,000-7,450 m) where the Indo-Australian oceanic plate subducts beneath the Sundaland continental plate.
properties.rock_type: Oceanic basalt, pelagic sediment, accretionary prism wedge
properties.evidence_description: Deep bathymetric V-shaped trough (>7,000 m), dipping Wadati-Benioff seismic zone, and accretionary forearc ridges (Mentawai, Enggano).
properties.evidence_significance: Primary convergent megathrust generating Indonesia's active volcanism, island arc uplift, and megathrust earthquakes/tsunamis.
properties.why_it_matters: The Sunda-Java Trench is one of Earth's most active convergent margins, driving regional plate tectonics and geohazards.
properties.location_province: Offshore Indian Ocean (Sumatra, Java, Bali, Nusa Tenggara)
properties.source: Bird (2003) 'An updated digital model of plate boundaries' & USGS Slab2 (Hayes et al., 2018)
properties.geometry_note: LineString trace digitized from authoritative global bathymetric trench axis data (Bird 2003 PB2002 dataset).

properties.name: Busur Vulkanik Sunda (Sunda Volcanic Arc Front Axis)
properties.description: Curvilinear chain of active Quaternary stratovolcanoes and magmatic arc complexes spanning Sumatra, Java, Bali, Lombok, Sumbawa, and Flores.
properties.rock_type: Calc-alkaline andesite, basaltic andesite, dacite, pyroclastic deposits
properties.evidence_description: Chain of over 100 active Quaternary volcanic centers positioned ~100-200 km above the subducting Indo-Australian slab.
properties.evidence_significance: Illustrates active subduction-induced mantle melting, crustal magma differentiation, and stratovolcano construction along Sundaland.
properties.why_it_matters: Forms the volcanic backbone of Western Indonesia, generating fertile soils, geothermal energy, and active volcanic hazards.
properties.source: Hamilton (1979) 'Tectonics of the Indonesian Region' (USGS Prof. Paper 1078) & Hall (2002)
properties.geometry_note: Representative volcanic front axis (interpretive cartographic convention connecting active volcanic centers, not an individual physical fault line).

properties.name: Sesar Lembang (Active Fault Trace)
properties.description: Active sinistral strike-slip fault with normal component extending ~29 km north of Bandung.
properties.evidence_description: Prominent north-facing fault scarp, stream offsets, and paleoseismic trenching evidence.
properties.evidence_significance: Slip rate ~3-6 mm/yr capable of generating M6.5-7.0 seismic events near Bandung metropolitan area.
properties.why_it_matters: Key active onshore fault in West Java with well-documented morphotectonic fault scarps.
properties.source: Badan Geologi ESDM & Daryono et al. (2019)
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of fault trace (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Sesar Cimandiri (Fault Zone)
properties.description: Major active oblique strike-slip fault zone extending from Pelabuhanratu Bay through Sukabumi to Padalarang.
properties.evidence_description: Morphotectonic valley linear, offset river terraces, and shallow crustal seismicity.
properties.evidence_significance: Major morphotectonic boundary separating northern Java fold belt from southern volcanic arc terrane.
properties.why_it_matters: Active fault zone responsible for periodic destructive shallow earthquakes in West Java.
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of fault zone (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Sesar Baribis (Thrust Belt Zone)
properties.description: Major back-arc thrust fault system in West-Central Java accommodating crustal shortening.
properties.evidence_description: North-verging thrust ramps, asymmetric folding, and GPS geodetic strain accumulation.
properties.evidence_significance: Accommodates back-arc shortening across Java with geodetic locking along southern Jakarta-Bogor corridor.
properties.why_it_matters: Critical active tectonic structure representing back-arc seismic hazard in northern Java.
properties.source: Badan Geologi ESDM & Koulali et al. (2017)
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of thrust zone (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Sesar Opak (Bantul Fault Zone)
properties.description: Active strike-slip fault zone along Opak river graben, source zone of 2006 Yogyakarta earthquake.
properties.rock_type: Alluvium, Merapi volcanic ash, Tertiary limestone basement
properties.evidence_description: Linear morphotectonic graben boundary and persistent shallow micro-seismicity.
properties.evidence_significance: Active crustal fault controlling intra-arc basin development and seismic hazard in Yogyakarta.
properties.why_it_matters: Site of the devastating 2006 Mw 6.3 Yogyakarta earthquake.
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of fault trace (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Sesar Besar Sumatra (Semangko Segment)
properties.description: Southernmost segment of Great Sumatran Fault entering Semangko Bay, accommodating oblique convergence.
properties.evidence_description: Prominent graben valley, strike-slip fault scarps, and geothermal spring alignments.
properties.evidence_significance: Key dextral strike-slip transform accommodating partitioned oblique subduction shear along Sumatra.
properties.why_it_matters: Demonstrates trench-parallel slip partitioning in oblique convergent margins.
properties.source: Badan Geologi ESDM & Sieh and Natawidjaja (2000)
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of fault segment (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Sesar Sorong (Fault System)
properties.description: Major left-lateral transform fault zone in Eastern Indonesia, accommodating Pacific-Australian plate motion.
properties.evidence_description: Transpressional ridges, pull-apart basins, and displaced continental fragments.
properties.evidence_significance: Key strike-slip structure transporting continental fragments from Australia/PNG westward into the Banda arc region.
properties.why_it_matters: Demonstrates rapid strike-slip terrane transport shaping Eastern Indonesia's complex tectonic mosaic.
properties.geometry_note: LineString representation of fault system (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Kompleks Mélange Ciletuh (Subduction Complex)
properties.description: Pre-Tertiary subduction mélange complex exposed at Ciletuh, West Java, featuring chaotic blocks of ophiolite, metamorphic schists, and deep-marine sediments.
properties.evidence_description: Exposed tectonic mélange blocks comprising oceanic crustal rocks embedded in sheared matrix.
properties.evidence_significance: Provides direct petrological evidence of ancient Cretaceous subduction accretion along Sundaland.
properties.why_it_matters: Ciletuh exposes Java's oldest basement rocks, allowing geoscientists to reconstruct Cretaceous plate subduction history.
properties.source: UNESCO Ciletuh-Palabuhanratu Geopark & Badan Geologi ESDM
properties.geometry_note: Polygon representation of complex boundary (interface visual convention).

properties.name: Kompleks Mélange Karangsambung (Ophiolite Complex)
properties.description: Cretaceous subduction accretionary complex exposing ophiolite sequence, pillow basalts, red chert, and tectonic mélange in Kebumen, Central Java.
properties.rock_type: Pillow Basalt, Red Chert, Serpentinite, Mica Schist
properties.evidence_description: Deep marine pillow basalts and radiolarian chert blocks structurally chaotic in scaly clay matrix.
properties.evidence_significance: Classic Indonesian tectonic benchmark site illustrating ancient subduction zone lithologies.
properties.why_it_matters: Karangsambung serves as Indonesia's open-air geological laboratory for studying subduction zone dynamics and ophiolite emplacement.
properties.source: Balai Informasi Geologi Karangsambung & Badan Geologi ESDM
properties.geometry_note: Polygon representation of complex boundary (interface visual convention).
